title: Charisma in a Crisis
coreMove: Give people the next steady action while your presence tells them the situation is being held.
sourcePressure: The source frames crisis as the highest-pressure application of the same triad: steadiness under urgency, authority plus reassurance, and warmth that preserves human contact without weakening action.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version becomes emergency leadership slogans. The useful version shows charisma as visible steadiness, human contact, and clear action when urgency could scatter everyone.

tryThisNow: Take command when things go wrong

exampleSpecs.domain: a children's theatre matinee after a lighting grid shorts and the house goes dark
exampleSpecs.audience: a stage manager who must calm children, parents, and crew at once
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the room exits safely without panic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she steps into the aisle with a battery lantern, gives one exit instruction, and tells the front row exactly who is coming next
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a battery lantern glowing against a dark velvet aisle

exampleSpecs.domain: a data center cooling failure during a payroll processing window
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead whose calm must guide technical and nontechnical staff
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether payroll runs while servers are protected from heat damage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he names the temperature threshold, assigns one person to payroll status and one to cooling vendors, then repeats the next checkpoint time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a server temperature dashboard flashing amber across a wall monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: a coastal ferry galley when a passenger has a severe allergic reaction
exampleSpecs.audience: a crew lead who needs authority without spreading fear
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether passengers clear space and the affected person receives help quickly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the crew lead kneels beside the passenger, points one server to the medical kit, and tells the watching passengers the next two actions in a level voice
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sealed medical kit sliding across a galley counter

exampleSpecs.domain: a sculpture foundry after a cracked mold threatens a hot bronze pour
exampleSpecs.audience: a shop lead balancing physical risk and apprentice fear
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the pour stops safely before anyone is burned
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she raises one hand, says stop once, points to the sand bucket and the marked line, then checks the apprentice's eyes before moving
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a hairline crack spreading across a ceramic shell mold

exampleSpecs.domain: a food co-op after a refrigeration failure spoils a vaccine clinic's snack supply
exampleSpecs.audience: a shift lead whose embarrassment could make the team scatter
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether volunteers protect guests, discard unsafe food, and keep the clinic moving
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the first scattered apology with the reset where she gives three calm assignments and personally moves the spoiled trays out of sight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a refrigerator thermometer resting above a tray of sweating yogurt cups

exampleSpecs.domain: a mountain hostel after a bus carrying guests fails to arrive before a snow closure
exampleSpecs.audience: a host who must keep stranded travelers informed without false certainty
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether guests conserve phone batteries, share rooms, and wait without rumor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the host realizes her first vague reassurance created rumor, then gathers everyone by the map, states what is known, and assigns the next update time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paper road-closure map weighted with a headlamp

skillTargets: choose crisis behavior that combines clear action with reassurance
distinguish charismatic steadiness from vague calm
analyze how authority and warmth prevent panic from spreading
evaluate whether a crisis response gives people a concrete next step

tryThisNowSpec: When something small goes wrong today, say what is known, give the next action, and name when you will update instead of filling the space with reassurance.
